why: Difference array for range updates: adding units to every slot in [start, end] is +units at start and -units just after end in a difference array. One prefix sum over the difference array then gives every slot's total, so each booking costs O(1) instead of O(length).
hints: Adding each booking slot by slot is O(n) per booking. What is the smallest change that describes 'add u from start to end'?
In a difference array d, d[start] += u and d[end+1] -= u. The prefix sum of d at slot x is exactly the total added to x.
Allocate d of size n+2, apply every booking in O(1), then one running sum over slots 1..n gives the answer. O(n + bookings).
pitfalls: Slots are 1-based and end is inclusive: the -u goes at end + 1.
Size the array n + 2 so end = n does not overflow.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ n ≤ 2 × 104
  • 1 ≤ bookings.length ≤ 2 × 104
  • bookings[i] = [start, end, units] with 1 ≤ start ≤ end ≤ n and 1 ≤ units ≤ 104
  • (Practice bounds; the source gives none.)
